headline: Chamath Palihapitiya calls Tesla-SpaceX merger 'very obvious industrial logic' — TSLA +0.4% overnight — in CNBC interview, Palihapitiya (early SpaceX investor via Founders Fund) said combining the two companies would create one capital structure and balance sheet for Musk's broader ambitions; he previously predicted SpaceX would reverse-merge into Tesla rather than pursue a traditional IPO; Jefferies simultaneously published a note saying SpaceX merger 'could hand shareholders a premium' with Musk retaining 55.3% voting control of the combined entity; both remarks reinforce that the SpaceX IPO (Jul 10, SPCX, $1.77T valuation) has removed the primary 'SpaceX is private' structural barrier to a deal; TSLA closed Tuesday at $396.18 (+0.40%); next major catalyst: Jul 22 Q2 earnings (Stocktwits / CNBC, Jul 15, 2026)

Jefferies raises TSLA PT to $400 (from $375), SpaceX merger could hand shareholders premium; Tesla Semi begins Chicago cold-weather pilot with Paper Transport — Jefferies cited Tesla's 'significant auto volume beat' (480K vs 406K consensus), raised Q2 EBIT to $1.45B / 5.1% margin, increased FY26 EBIT 4% to $6.2B; group revenue seen at $28.7B; Q2 capex $6.9B; still expects $7.5B FCF outflow; Jefferies says multi-year growth/earnings deterioration 'beginning to reverse'; Tesla Semi Chicago pilot with Paper Transport targets 500-mile cold-climate range validation — success would expand addressable market to harsh-winter regions; maintains Hold (Jefferies / Stocktwits, Jul 14–15, 2026)

Q2 2026 earnings: options market implies 7.6% move on July 22 — Wall Street consensus EPS $0.52/share (+30% YoY) on revenue of $25.81B (+14.8% YoY); Morgan Stanley (Andrew Percoco) raised PT to $417 from $415, maintains Equal Weight; bears focused on $7.5B FCF outflow and $25B capex cycle; bulls watching for (1) automotive gross margin ex-credits vs Q1's 21.1% print, (2) first Optimus unit count, (3) Cybercab commercial launch timeline, (4) FSD ARR growth; TSLA at $396.10 is sitting below the consensus PT average of $425.23; 7 analysts revised Q2 estimates higher since Jul 13; overall analyst rating remains 'Buy' but with cautious optimism at current valuation; July 22 is the first earnings call where Optimus production units will be on the balance sheet (TipRanks / Blockonomi / Morgan Stanley, Jul 15, 2026)

Tesla Q2 2026 energy deployment: 13.5 GWh (+53% QoQ) — record Q2 in company history, confirms Q1 8.8 GWh miss was timing not demand — closest prior Q2 was Q3 2023's 12.5 GWh; Megapack backlog remains 2–3 years deep; at Q2 run-rate Tesla is tracking toward ~54 GWh full-year 2026 vs ~48 GWh consensus; energy gross margins to be revealed in Jul 22 Q2 financials; energy recovery removes a key bear narrative from Q1 and directly supports the $10B+ energy revenue thesis for full-year 2026; Model Y L launch (Jul 3) and Optimus ramp also add new 2H revenue streams (teslaoracle.com / Tesla IR, Jul 15, 2026)

EXCLUSIVE: Tesla HW4 consumer vehicles run distilled FSD models developed first on Cybercab hardware — sources confirm Tesla trains massive 'teacher' neural networks for the more powerful Cybercab compute, then distills them into smaller 'student' models for HW4 consumer vehicles; Cybercab's extra compute headroom serves as the frontier FSD development sandbox for each software generation; HW4 confirmed sufficient for unsupervised FSD via distillation while HW3 is not; reveals clear AI architecture hierarchy driving Tesla's moat: every Cybercab-tier improvement cascades to the entire consumer fleet; directly explains why Cybercab's hardware investment pays dividends across all vehicles, not just the robotaxi fleet (notateslaapp, Jul 14, 2026)

Tesla Cybercab confirmed giving employee rides at Giga Texas as of July 10 — Tesla official X account posted video of production Cybercab (no steering wheel, no pedals) autonomously picking up and dropping off employees in the Giga Texas outbound lot; basenor: 'Tesla has quietly crossed a line that no major automaker has crossed before'; Electrek raised ambiguity on whether operations are parking-lot-only or extend to public roads; a clip of Robotaxi app vent-control UI briefly visible in the original post was later edited out by Tesla, prompting speculation on app feature depth; first time purpose-built Level 4 hardware has transported actual passengers at commercial-adjacent scale; key operational bridge between production ramp and public commercial launch ahead of Jul 22 Q2 earnings (basenor / notateslaapp / Electrek, Jul 10–13, 2026)

FSD v14.3.5 first Teslascope-recorded drive completes 100% autonomously — Teslascope confirmed the very first logged drive on build 2026.20.6.6 was completed entirely on FSD with zero interventions; early user reports broadly positive on the new camera-preview-at-any-time feature; basenor confirmed rollout continuing; 100% completion rate on first logged drive is a notable early data point ahead of Jul 22 Q2 earnings where FSD reliability metrics will be a focus (basenor / Teslascope, Jul 14, 2026)

Tesla Robotaxi fleet near-flawless in new NHTSA safety report (Apr 15–Jun 16) — Tesla logged only 1 incident in 62 days of unsupervised Austin operation: a zero-fault event where a stationary Robotaxi obeying a red arrow signal was rear-ended by a human-driven pickup truck; Zoox logged +6 incidents, Waymo +191 in the same period; data not normalized by fleet miles, but confirms Tesla's Austin operational envelope is performing at extremely high reliability; directly challenges the '4x human crash rate' framing from earlier NHTSA filings; strongest safety data point yet heading into Jul 22 Q2 earnings (notateslaapp / NHTSA filings, Jul 13, 2026)

Tesla FSD inches toward Italy approval — Tesla submitted FSD homologation paperwork to Italy's Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport; General Director Servedio Gaetano confirmed on LinkedIn the filing is in active analysis; Italy applying Netherlands fast-track recognition path; follows Belgium, Denmark, Estonia, and Lithuania approvals since May; Italy is the 6th EU country to formally engage with FSD post-Netherlands clearance and the bloc's 4th-largest market; as each EU approval uses the Netherlands as foundational clearance, incremental approvals are coming faster; EU TCMV vote window still open in July (notateslaapp / TeslaNewswire / MirkoMontagna0 on X, Jul 13, 2026)

Tesla tears down Model S/X production lines at Fremont for Optimus — official @gigafactories X account posts time-lapse: 'End of an era: Decommissioning the original Model S & X assembly line in just 46 days'; footage shows massive robotic arms removed, structural foundations cleared, concrete floor completely repoured; AI chief Ashok Elluswamy: 'Big shoes to fill, but I'm confident Optimus will not disappoint!!'; Elon Musk confirms first Optimus production line 'successfully put in place' at Fremont; initial output will be 'quite slow'; late-July/August production start target on schedule; first official Optimus unit count expected on Jul 22 Q2 earnings call (notateslaapp / @gigafactories / Musk on X, Jul 13–14, 2026)
